LESSON: FUEL CONSERVATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.3: Fuel Conservation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Fuel Conservation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does reducing fuel wastage conserve our resources?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify types of fuels used at home

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: FUEL CONSERVATION
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Fuel Conservation helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: FUEL CONSERVATION
Study Fuel Conservation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify types of fuels used at home

What this means
In this part you learn to identify types of fuels used at home. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify types of fuels used at home.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Fuel Conservation” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify types of fuels used at home. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Fuel Conservation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Fuel Conservation” around your school. (skill: identify types of fuels used at home)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Fuel Conservation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify types of fuels used at home.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Fuel Conservation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Fuel Conservation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Fuel Conservation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does reducing fuel wastage conserve our resources?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Fuel Conservation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify types of fuels used at home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
